findings.area: Requirements traceability / reconciliation coverage (ADR-012 repair guarantee)
findings.description: The task 6.9 scheduled (periodic + manual) and post-scan reconciliation triggers exist, are bounded, and are real Jellyfin 12 extension points (independently confirmed below), but their coverage of the configured scope is capped by the bounded work queue and does not rotate, so the documented repair guarantee is delivered only for a bounded prefix of the scope. LibraryReconciliationService always starts at startIndex 0 and enumerates candidates in a deterministic order (SortName ascending, JellyfinMediaLibraryEnumerator.cs:61); it continues enumerating after a rejected hint (LibraryReconciliationService.cs:154), and LibraryWorkQueue.TryEnqueue drops the hint once pending work has reached QueueCapacity (default 512, OperationalLimits.cs:38; LibraryWorkQueue.cs:166-171). The producer performs no external I/O per item (in-memory paging only) while the four-worker consumer performs a provider HTTP read per work item (LibraryWorkWorker.cs:28; MetadataReconciliationProcessor.cs:139-142 has no freshness short-circuit before the read), so a run over a scope larger than QueueCapacity saturates the queue early and drops the tail; the next periodic/manual/post-scan run re-enumerates from index 0 in the same order and therefore re-covers the same prefix rather than the dropped items. For a configured scope larger than QueueCapacity (realistic once BadgeEpisodePosters is enabled) an Arr-side metadata change on an item outside the prefix that raises no Jellyfin item event and is covered by no webhook is still never repaired by the scheduled/post-scan path - the exact scenario the previous phase-review HIGH finding described and that ADR-012 (decisions.md:1473-1477, 1500-1501) and architecture section 8 (architecture.md:462-464) promise the periodic reconciliation will repair. No unsafe behaviour results (hints stay bounded and coalesced and the worker re-reads and re-validates current state), and the task 6.9 worker report records the overflow drop as a known limitation, but its framing ('the next periodic, manual, or post-scan run re-reads current state') does not disclose that each run re-covers the same prefix, and neither the PLANS.md Phase 7 deferral list nor the architecture/ADR wording records the coverage bound.

findings.area: Provider API efficiency / GOALS 'avoid unnecessary API requests' (tracked deferral wording)
findings.description: Task 6.9 adds a full-scope producer on top of a pipeline that still performs a full provider inventory read per work item: RadarrMetadataReader.ReadAsync calls GetMoviesAsync (whole movie inventory) and then GetMovieFilesAsync, the Sonarr reader is structured the same way, and MetadataReconciliationProcessor performs the provider read for every work item with no freshness or revision-token short-circuit before it. Before 6.9 the volume of such reads was bounded by the rate of actual Jellyfin item events and webhook deliveries; now every media-library scan and every 12-hour periodic run enqueues up to QueueCapacity eligible items, each of which re-reads the whole provider inventory. This is efficiency only (bounded, cancellation-aware, and now concurrency-limited), it does not affect correctness or safety, and it is correctly tracked as a Phase 7 deferral rather than presented as solved. However, the deferral wording still describes the gap as 'a large library scan performs one full provider-library read per event', which understates the post-6.9 volume, and Phase 6 acceptance criterion 1 is correctly marked as only partially met in PLANS.md.

findings.description: DynamicConcurrencyLimiter resolves the effective limit from the current configuration snapshot on every acquisition, so a limit increase is observed by new callers, but a caller already suspended on the limiter's signal is not proactively woken when the limit grows; it is admitted only when the next permit release signals. With today's fixed startup limits and the bounded caller set (the four-worker pool, where every permit holder is guaranteed to release before acquiring any other boundary), the worst case is one operation of added latency and no stall, so there is no impact on Phase 6; the focused test DynamicLimiterReadsTheLimitOnEachAcquisition exercises growth through a new acquisition and therefore matches the implemented behaviour. The nuance becomes observable only once runtime configuration replacement is wired, which is a tracked Phase 7 deferral: an administrator raising provider or render concurrency would not immediately admit already-waiting work.

requirements_checked: Phase 6 AC1 'Unchanged metadata and source state do not repeatedly fetch, render, or publish work unnecessarily': partially satisfied. Render and publication remain fingerprint-gated (ArtworkRegenerationPlanner) and queued work is coalesced, but every work item still fetches provider metadata because MetadataReconciliationProcessor reads the provider before any freshness/fingerprint comparison, and task 6.9's full-scope triggers now enqueue up to QueueCapacity such reads per run (LOW finding; correctly recorded as partial in PLANS.md:2437-2440 and as a Phase 7 deferral).
Phase 6 AC2 'A changed Arr file, source image, badge configuration, or renderer version produces the required new fingerprint and render result': satisfied, unchanged by 6.9.
Phase 6 AC3 'Temporary provider outages use bounded last-known-good state only within policy, then leave the current usable artwork unchanged': satisfied, unchanged by 6.9.

Phase 6 AC4 'Queue overflow and slow providers never block Jellyfin library event delivery indefinitely': satisfied. Task 6.9 uses the same non-blocking IWorkHintSink; a reconciliation run can drop hints under overflow but never blocks an enqueue caller, and the post-scan/scheduled callers are not Jellyfin event delivery.

Phase 6 AC5 'Restart or cancellation cannot publish partial state or partial image output': satisfied. The reconciliation checks cancellation before and inside each page and between pages, checks the durable lifecycle fence before the run and between pages, and only enqueues hints (no direct provider/render/publish work); a cancelled or fenced run returns a bounded Cancelled/Fenced result and enqueues nothing further, leaving durable state authoritative.

Phase 6 AC6 'Plugin cache and provenance entries are bounded where applicable, versioned, recoverable, and free of credentials': satisfied, unchanged by 6.9. The new work hint carries only the Jellyfin item id, the bounded reason and the safe configuration version; no credential, path, or provider payload was added anywhere in the new code or tests.

summary: Phase 6 is complete and the previous review's HIGH finding is genuinely resolved, so the phase is approved to hand to the next phase with the MEDIUM coverage item tracked. All nine authoritative tasks (6.1-6.9) are complete, each has worker and reviewer evidence and its own commit, the commit order matches the execution order exactly, the order is internally consistent with the documented dependencies, and the working tree is clean with no unrelated changes. I independently reproduced the environment build (0 warnings / 0 errors against pinned Jellyfin 12.0.0 / net10.0) and the full suite (Failed 0, Passed 1197, Skipped 58, Total 1255) plus the focused 6.9 filter (27/27, no skips). HIGH resolution: task 6.9 adds a bounded, cancellation-aware, fence-respecting LibraryReconciliationService that pages the configured Movie/Episode scope through a new IMediaLibraryEnumerator boundary, filters each page through the existing identity/eligibility boundaries, yields between batches, and enqueues only the same bounded LibraryWorkHint work as every other trigger. I did not accept the discovery claims from the report: I inspected the pinned Jellyfin 12.0.0 XML contracts (IScheduledTask, ILibraryPostScanTask, ILibraryManager.AddParts) and fetched the pinned host source revision to confirm ApplicationHost.Init/DiscoverTypes/GetComposablePartAssemblies, FindParts -> CreatePlugins then AddParts(GetExports<ILibraryPostScanTask>), RunStartupTasksAsync -> AddTasks(GetExports<IScheduledTask>), ScheduledTaskWorker's default-trigger/IntervalTicks handling and cancellation classification, and LibraryManager.RunPostScanTasks' invocation from PerformLibraryValidation (with non-cancellation failures logged rather than rethrown). The architecture's refresh-trigger set (item events, post-scan, manual/periodic scheduled, webhooks) now matches the implementation, and ADR-012's periodic-reconciliation guarantee is backed by a real producer, subject to the coverage finding below. MEDIUM concurrency finding: resolved - the ADR-004 provider per-connection/global and render limits are enforced at the real provider-read and render boundaries through bounded, cancellation-aware limiters resolved from the current snapshot per operation, with tests that measure a real concurrent peak at and never above the configured value; I verified the decorators are the only production path for those boundaries and that permit acquisition order (global then per-connection, permits released before the per-subject gate) makes a deadlock cycle impossible and that the two lock domains cannot invert. The remaining MEDIUM/LOW items are either resolved or explicitly tracked for Phase 7 and not presented as solved: the provider catalogue cache, runtime configuration replacement wiring and metrics/status surface are recorded in the PLANS.md Post-V1 backlog and docs/implementation-readiness.md, and Phase 6 acceptance criterion 1 is correctly marked as partially met. The main remaining issue (MEDIUM) is that the new triggers' coverage is capped by the bounded work queue and does not rotate: each run enumerates from index 0 in a deterministic order and re-covers the same first ~QueueCapacity (default 512) eligible items, so an Arr-side change outside that prefix that raises no Jellyfin item event and is covered by no webhook is still not repaired - the exact scenario the previous HIGH described. It is safe and bounded, and it does not block the phase, but the coverage bound must be recorded in the architecture/ADR wording and carried into Phase 7 (rotating cursor, stale-only enqueue, or an equivalent) rather than living only in the task report. LOW findings are the understated deferral wording for provider-fetch volume, two stale documentation statements (implementation-readiness status line; architecture line 735), the limiter's non-proactive wake on limit growth (relevant only once Phase 7 wires runtime configuration replacement), and the unchanged Phase 5/host-validation and quarantine carry-forwards. Security and safety re-checked: no secrets in the new code or tests, the new trigger is an internal bounded producer with no new route, authoritative state is never evicted as cache, hints are re-validated by the worker, and cancellation or a raised fence cannot enqueue further work or publish partial output. Phase 5 carry-forwards remain correctly tracked for Phase 7, with no regression introduced by this phase.
